title: Testing nature, not just arguing
question: What turned thinking about nature into physics?
hook: For about two thousand years, the best-known physics was argued out rather than tested.
idea: Physics became its own science when people tested ideas with experiments and measurement instead of relying on argument alone.

beats.prompt: Two thinkers want to know the rules of motion. One reasons from first principles and never checks. The other runs experiments and measures results. Whose method made physics a separate science?

choices.label: The one who reasons without checking
choices.feedback: Aristotle's logical arguments were influential for about two millennia, but they did not rely on experimental verification.

choices.label: The one who experiments and measures
The one who names the stars after gods
choices.feedback: Naming and worshipping stars belongs to early astronomy, not to the method that split physics off.

beats.explain: Physics became a separate science when early modern Europeans used experimental and quantitative methods to discover its laws.

beats.prompt: Put these moments in physics history in order
items: Thales and others reject non-naturalistic explanations
Aristotle writes his work on Physics
John Philoponus challenges the Aristotelian approach
Thermodynamics, mechanics and electromagnetics match a wide variety of observations
beats.explain: Natural philosophy began in Greece in the Archaic period, Aristotle wrote in the 4th century BC, Philoponus in the sixth century, and the classical theories matched observations by the end of the 19th century.

beats.prompt: Match each person to what the sentences credit them with
beats.explain: Each of these thinkers moved the study of nature forward in a different way, from atoms to elements to light to calculus.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning about Aristotle's physics is wrong. Which?
steps: Each of the four elements has a natural place, with fire at the top.
A flame on the ground is out of place, so it moves up toward its place.
This explains the flame, so the theory is proven and needs no experiment.
Therefore the theory is a reasonable framework to build on.
beats.explain: Explaining one example does not verify a theory. Aristotle's approach did not rely on experimental verification of deduced statements, and it is entirely superseded today.
